questions.explanation: Past continuous for the longer background action interrupted by the phone.
questions.q: While I ___ dinner, the phone rang.

questions.explanation: Past simple for completed actions in a story sequence.
questions.q: She ___ the door and walked into the dark room.

questions.explanation: Past perfect shows the film started before we arrived.
questions.q: When we got to the cinema, the film ___.

questions.explanation: Past continuous for the weather in progress at that past moment.
questions.q: It ___ heavily when we left the house.

questions.explanation: Past perfect continuous for an activity continuing up to a past moment.
questions.q: He was tired because he ___ all day.

questions.explanation: Past continuous sets the background scene in a narrative.
questions.q: The sun ___ and the birds were singing.

questions.explanation: 'While' + past continuous for the longer action, past simple for the interrupting event.
options: While I walked home, it started to rain.
While I was walking home, it started to rain.
While I had walked home, it started to rain.
While I walk home, it started to rain.
questions.q: Which sentence is correct?

questions.explanation: Past perfect continuous for a long activity before another past event.
questions.q: She ___ for two hours before she found her keys.

questions.explanation: Past continuous for an action in progress when another event happened.
questions.q: They ___ TV when I arrived.

questions.explanation: Past perfect = had + past participle: 'had left'.
questions.q: She suddenly realised she ___ her passport at home.

questions.explanation: Past simple for the short completed action that interrupted the continuous one.
questions.q: I ___ my arm while I was playing football.

questions.explanation: Past continuous for a parallel ongoing action in the past.
questions.q: The children ___ noisily while the teacher was talking.

questions.explanation: Past continuous for the ongoing action, past simple for the sudden event.
options: He was driving too fast when the accident happened.
He drove too fast when the accident was happening.
He had driven too fast when the accident was happening.
He drives too fast when the accident happened.
questions.q: Which of the following sentences is correct?

questions.explanation: 'By the time' takes the past perfect for the earlier event.
questions.q: By the time we arrived, everyone ___ home.

questions.explanation: Past continuous asks about an action in progress at a specific past time.
questions.q: What ___ at 8 o'clock last night?

questions.explanation: Past perfect with 'already' for the earlier of two past events.
questions.q: The match ___ when we turned on the TV.

questions.explanation: After 'was', use verb+ing: 'was working', not 'was work'.
options: She was cooking while he was working.
She was cooking while he was work.
She had cooked before he arrived.
questions.q: Which sentence is WRONG?

questions.explanation: Past perfect = had + past participle: 'had forgotten'.
questions.q: He ___ his keys, so he went back to the office.

questions.explanation: Past continuous for the action in progress when the lights went out.
questions.q: She ___ a shower when the lights went out.

questions.explanation: Past simple for the interrupting event, past continuous for the ongoing background action.
options: They were arriving while we had dinner.
They arrive while we were having dinner.
They had arrived while we had dinner.
They arrived while we were having dinner.
questions.q: Choose the grammatically correct sentence.
